clue.text: Magnetism as Mum does the housework?

parts.note: one who does the housework is a char, so the words are read as 'is char', put in the order the letters run
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother's charm is wondered about as she does the cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mum does the housework' as 'char is Ma': a CHAR is a cleaning lady, so the phrase becomes CHAR IS MA, with the question mark flagging the odd reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm that draws others to a person is a figurative kind of personal attraction.

clue.text: Giant from flanks of cavalry sounds like a horse

indicators.note: the flanks are the outer sides, so the first and last letters of cavalry are taken

parts.note: a horse's hooves clop, so it clops

explanation.surface: A giant emerges from the edges of a cavalry unit, sounding like a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' is no homophone here: it is the hoof noise CLOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-eyed giants of Greek myth, met by Odysseus, are of this kind.

clue.text: Lines are written up for everybody

indicators.note: in a down clue written up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: L is lines, doubled as LL for plural
an are is a metric unit of area, A

explanation.surface: Lines are composed for everyone to read.
explanation.walkthrough: LL and A, read upwards in this down clue, give ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody means every person, the whole lot of them.

clue.text: Hesitating, I slip when lifting very old instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: to err is to slip or make a mistake
so means very, as in 'so good'
the lute is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates, saying they slip while lifting an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when lifting' turns ERR to RRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An irresolute person is undecided and hesitant, unable to commit.

clue.text: Communication means some diagrams must be cropped

indicators.note: the outer letters of the phrase are trimmed away, leaving a run within it

explanation.surface: A note on communication says some diagrams must be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across soME DIAgrams once the ends are cropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Press, radio and television are the means of mass communication.

clue.text: Airline in the money for this quarter in African city

indicators.note: the airline's letters are placed inside the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: An airline is paid for flying travellers to a North African district.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways; 'for this' is a link pointing at the city quarter defined at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the old walled quarter of a North African city such as Algiers.

clue.text: Way off, keeping right off course

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation inside them
off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of way are muddled

explanation.surface: Way off, a vessel keeps to the right but drifts off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WAY to AWY, and 'keeping' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awry has gone astray or is askew, not on its proper course.

clue.text: Abruptly put goods aboard boat, mostly from South Asian republic

parts.note: bang means suddenly, as in 'bang on time'
to lade is to load cargo

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: Goods are suddenly loaded onto a vessel, chiefly from a South Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SHIP to SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladeshi is the adjective for things or people from Bangladesh.

clue.text: The man's blue, eventful past

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a Tory

explanation.surface: A man's sad past was full of events.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative party colour in Britain, so a Tory is a blue.
explanation.definitionFit: History is the record of past events, a sequence of happenings.

clue.text: In addition to a balloon, a second

parts.note: to balloon is to swell

explanation.surface: A balloon is mentioned along with a moment of time.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means besides or together with, adding one thing to another.

clue.text: City that flanks Rocky Mountains pass, otherwise trouble breaks out

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll miss it'
ado is fuss or trouble
springs means leaps or breaks out

explanation.surface: A city in the mountains warns that if a pass is not used, trouble will erupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like part of the scenery, but it is COL; the city sits at the foot of the Rockies in the US state of Colorado.
explanation.definitionFit: This Colorado city lies at the eastern foot of the Rockies, beside Pikes Peak.

clue.text: One hanging around too long finished ahead of persistent horse

indicators.note: the first piece is placed before the second in the answer

parts.note: over means ended or finished
a stayer is a horse with stamina for long races

explanation.surface: A loiterer has finished in front of a stubborn racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who outstays a visa or welcome lingers beyond the permitted time.

clue.text: With bends the same question occurs in terrible neuralgia

indicators.note: the abbreviation for question sits inside the rearranged letters
terrible signals the letters of neuralgia are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether identical twinges come with awful nerve pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bends' suggests the bends of a diver or a river, but here it means the corners of a figure, all at equal angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Equiangular describes a figure whose angles, or bends, are all equal.

clue.text: Remove each doubling in regrettably very high voice

indicators.note: each letter that appears twice in the phrase loses one of its pair

parts.note: all too means regrettably very, as in 'all too common'

explanation.surface: A singer is told to cut out repetitions in an unfortunately shrill voice.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL TOO has a double L and a double O; removing one of each leaves ALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a high male voice or the lowest female voice, a vocal register.

clue.text: Frenchwoman's standard that is lined with endless brown

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is surrounds the trimmed colour

parts.note: ie (id est) means that is

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: sienna is a reddish-brown pigment

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's flag is trimmed with a brown border.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Frenchwoman is a link meaning 'is'; ie stands for the Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parisienne is a woman from Paris, the French capital.

clue.text: Dirty metal found in molluscs

indicators.note: the metal's symbol sits inside the word for the molluscs

parts.note: squid (plural same as singular) are molluscs
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Grime and metal turn up inside shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid describes surroundings that are filthy and neglected.

clue.text: Split region's mail data after corruption

indicators.note: corrupted data has its contents scrambled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Email data split up after file corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a verb, but it is the Croatian port city; capitalised at the start of the clue, it hides its proper noun status.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is the coastal region of Croatia whose main city is Split.

clue.text: Period primarily inserted to manage a year

definitions.text: Period primarily inserted to manage a year

indicators.note: that first letter goes inside the word for manage

parts.note: to lead is to manage or direct

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word Period is used

explanation.surface: A stretch of time is slipped in to keep the calendar year in order.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside LEAD, followed by A and Y; the whole clue also describes the answer, an extra day inserted to keep the year in step.
explanation.definitionFit: February 29th is the extra day added in leap years to keep the calendar aligned with the sun.

clue.text: Fossil fuel holds while tons found at seaboards

indicators.note: the fuel's letters surround the other pieces

parts.note: coal is a fossil fuel
as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: Coal is kept while tonnes are discovered along the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal means situated on or near the shore, where land meets the sea.

clue.text: Proficient secretary intercepts telegram

indicators.note: the secretary cuts into the telegram, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: a cable is a telegram
a PA is a personal assistant or secretary

explanation.surface: A skilled secretary intercepts an incoming telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means competent, able to do things well.

clue.text: Cut takes place in New Cross

indicators.note: the short word goes inside the rearranged letters
new suggests the letters of the word cross are made into something new

parts.note: is means exists or takes place

explanation.surface: A stabbing is reported in the New Cross district.
explanation.walkthrough: New Cross is a district of south-east London, but here 'New' is an anagram signal working on Cross alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To scissor is to cut with shears, a verb formed from the tool.

clue.text: Pity about Telegraph pioneer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Samuel Morse pioneered the electric telegraph and its code

explanation.surface: A newspaper sympathises over a telegraph inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' suggests the British newspaper, but it is the electric telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity in the sense of regret ('it's a pity') matches remorse, sorrow for a wrong.

clue.text: Quiet period or episode in 8

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A calm interval or a passing episode in the story is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to 8 Down, HISTORY: an episode in history is a page of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A page in history is an episode, as in 'a glorious page in our nation's story'.

clue.text: Zeal whipped up maniac's fit

indicators.note: whipped up means stirred, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A madman's frenzy stirs up fanatical enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is part of the fodder here: MANIACSFIT rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanatical zeal is extreme enthusiasm, the passion of the zealot.

clue.text: Energy is extracted from a base block of iron

parts.note: an is a form of the indefinite article a

indicators.note: the energy letter is pulled out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: base means wicked or evil
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy is drawn from a foundation made of an iron block.
explanation.walkthrough: AN EVIL (a base thing) loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is a heavy iron block on which a smith hammers metal.

clue.text: Pilgrim overturning principal features of Islam, Judaism and Hinduism

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning means the letters read upwards
the principal or first letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A pilgrim rejects the main features of three great religions.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters I, J, A, H, read upwards, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca.

clue.text: It's used in dressing light wood recorder with slender stem and paper back

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood
a mic (microphone) records sound
a vine is a slender climbing stem

indicators.note: back means the word for paper is turned round

parts.note: rag is slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Light wood, a recorder, a slender stalk and a newspaper are listed as dressing materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's clue was cut short in the held text. 'back' turns RAG to GAR. 'Dressing' suggests clothes or bandages, but it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark Italian vinegar is a common ingredient of salad dressings.

clue.text: Sticky stuff is to leave a ring

parts.note: to go is to leave
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Sticky stuff is to leave a ring behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is a sticky or slimy substance.

clue.text: A bug for Americans to eavesdrop

definitions.meaning: in US usage, to listen in secretly on a conversation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' also hints at listening devices, tying the two senses together.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a pincered insect and, in American English, a verb meaning to listen in.

clue.text: Played jazz for audience, bending tone to make this?

definitions.text: Played jazz for audience, bending tone to make this?

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard, so the past tense of blowing a horn is taken by its sound

parts.note: jazz players blow their horns, so played is blew

indicators.note: bending means the letters of the word tone are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A jazz musician bends a note in performance to create a particular sound.
explanation.walkthrough: BLEW sounds like BLUE, and 'bending' rearranges TONE to NOTE; the whole clue describes a flattened, bent pitch in jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: In jazz and blues a slightly flattened, bent pitch is the characteristic expressive note.
